clue.text: Autumn turns out to provide unexpected gains

indicators.note: the turns sit out on the edges, wrapped round the season rather than beside it

blocks.note: winds as a verb means turns or twists
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: The arrival of autumn somehow brings unexpected profits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sneaks in windfalls of fallen fruit, apt for autumn, so the answer hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is a sudden piece of good fortune, typically money nobody was expecting.

clue.text: Revolver we'll hear

indicators.note: hear tells the solver to go by how the preceding words sound when spoken

blocks.note: the contraction we'll is pronounced like a word for a turning disc

explanation.surface: Someone promises that we will hear a gun go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' wants to be a pistol; here it is simply anything that revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a thing that turns round an axle, so it literally is a revolver.

clue.text: No A-team member getting ninety not out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a lesser player scores ninety not out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ninety not out' reads as a cricket score, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on ninety and not.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonentity is an unimportant person, the opposite of someone in the first team or elite group.

clue.text: Brawl with nobody facing charges?

blocks.note: first meaning: a disorganised fight in which everyone joins
second meaning, read literally: no charge for anyone, free of cost to everyone

explanation.surface: A punch-up where, oddly, no one ends up arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like criminal charges after a fight; the second reading needs charges as prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a chaotic fight, and taken word by word it describes something costing nothing for anyone.

clue.text: Female in meadow allowed a bit of advertising material?

indicators.note: in places the female inside, between the field and the permission

blocks.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
F is the standard abbreviation for female
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A woman standing in a field has been permitted some promotional material.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out to advertise or inform, a small piece of publicity.

clue.text: Drug present in diets or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these letters appear in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that a banned drug may lurk in your diet, or elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Steroids are a class of drugs, including the performance-enhancing kind used by athletes.

clue.text: Carry minute emblem that's venerated

blocks.note: to tote is to carry
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to carry a tiny sacred symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny, but it is the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal revered as a sacred symbol by a group or clan.

clue.text: Skirt for opponent of apartheid

blocks.note: first meaning: a ballerina's short stiff skirt
second meaning: Archbishop Desmond, the South African campaigner against racial segregation

explanation.walkthrough: Desmond Tutu was the Nobel-winning South African archbishop who fought apartheid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a ballet dancer's frilly garment and a famous anti-apartheid churchman.

clue.text: Financial arrangement tied up, so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said points to a word that sounds like the preceding phrase when spoken

blocks.note: trussed means tied up, as a chicken before roasting

explanation.surface: A deal said to have all its money tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied up' sounds like money being locked away, which suits the surface, but it is the sense of bound with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust is a legal arrangement where assets are held and managed for someone's benefit.

clue.text: Brand has half-term rush

indicators.note: half asks for only part of the following word, here its opening two letters

blocks.note: a make is a brand of product
taken as written
the first half of term

explanation.surface: A school-holiday picture of a label rushing out at half-term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-term' reads as the school break, but it means half of the word term.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is an idiom for hurrying, exactly what rushing is.

clue.text: Wise man's last seen in great lake

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word before it
seen in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America
the final letter of man

explanation.surface: A sage is spotted at a big lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise man' reads as a sage, but Wise is the surname of comedian Ernie Wise, of the British double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the straight man of a famous British comedy duo, so his first name answers Wise.

clue.text: Gobsmacked as we shot by lorry

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters before it come apart and reform

blocks.note: taken as written
truck is another word for a lorry

explanation.surface: Stunned as a lorry rushes past us.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue omits its count, which is (9).
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly astonished, the same as being filled with awe.

clue.text: Going on a bit, chap who's a poet

blocks.note: something long goes on a bit
a fellow is a chap

explanation.surface: A long-winded man who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of Hiawatha and Paul Revere's Ride.

clue.text: Produce artwork that's required by supermarket chain

indicators.note: required by suggests the answer is contained within the following phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An art piece commissioned by a big grocery company.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to make a picture by cutting lines into metal with acid, a printmaking art.

clue.text: Queer old dean, say, breaking no promises

indicators.note: breaking smashes the phrase so its letters can be rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric old college head who won't make promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queer old dean' is the classic swap attributed to Rev. William Spooner for 'dear old Queen'; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a famous instance of swapping initial sounds, the slip named after Spooner.

clue.text: In novel form I'm great detective

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boastful sleuth announcing his greatness in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' fits the detective-story surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional French police inspector, the hero of many novels.

clue.text: Manly man (clue is cryptic)

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so the letters are hidden in a jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the bracket

explanation.surface: A setter's aside that the clue for manly is a cryptic one.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a comment about the puzzle, but its words, with man, are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Masculine describes qualities traditionally associated with men, the same as manly.

clue.text: Shows given low grades by old people

blocks.note: D and E are poor marks in exams
the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland

explanation.surface: A school report full of poor marks handed out by elderly teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' suggests pensioners; it is an ancient tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to show or portray something in a picture or words.

clue.text: Janitor, a conscientious type?

blocks.note: first meaning: a building's custodian
second meaning, read literally: someone who takes care

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a playful literal reading of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the job title for a building custodian and, split up, describes a person who is careful.

clue.text: A heavenly shade

blocks.note: surface reading: a divine ghost or spirit in the afterlife
setter's reading: the colour of a clear sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' tempts the solver toward a ghost in heaven; it means a colour, and heavenly means of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the pale blue of a cloudless sky, so literally a colour from the heavens.

clue.text: Selected passage right in bar

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: bar as a preposition means except
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A chosen extract read aloud in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it means 'apart from'.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract chosen from a longer text, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Company blocking sudden increase? That causes great suffering

indicators.note: blocking places the firm in the middle, in the way of the other word

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rise
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm standing in the way of a boom proves a terrible affliction.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is anything, such as a plague or tyrant, that brings widespread misery.

clue.text: Head of state bumped off expert

indicators.note: head of asks for just the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of state
bumped off is slang for killed

explanation.surface: An assassination: a national leader is murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' reads as a president or monarch, but it means only the first letter of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled and expert both describe someone highly proficient at something.

clue.text: Vessels of American and British navy going in

indicators.note: going in puts the second item inside the first

blocks.note: US is short for American
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Ships of two navies in an allied operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' and 'navy' suggest ships, but the vessels here are containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, and vessel is a general word for a container.

clue.text: Dark period for famous nurse missing in gale

indicators.note: missing means the words after it are absent from the name

blocks.note: Florence Nightingale, the Crimean War nurse
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A nurse is lost in a storm overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the hours of darkness between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Breaking a code, Clint appears in Western

indicators.note: breaking smashes the letters so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Clint Eastwood cracks a code in a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests a cowboy film starring Clint, but it is the adjective meaning of the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Occidental means relating to the West, the opposite of oriental.

clue.text: Cover over very large leisure facilities

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Covering up oversized swimming baths.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a place for recreation.

clue.text: Bionic man ignoring the odds is old American

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means skipping letters in odd positions and keeping the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A cyborg defies the odds and turns out to be an ancient American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring the odds' sounds like beating long chances; it means dropping odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the people of a pre-Columbian empire in the Andes of South America.

clue.text: Popular officer, more often than not

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In general is an idiom meaning usually or as a rule.

clue.text: Annoyed Irish king — extremely exasperated

indicators.note: extremely asks for only the extremes, the outermost letters of the next word

blocks.note: Ir is the abbreviation for Irish
K is king in chess and cards
the first and last letters of exasperated

explanation.surface: An Irish monarch who is very fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for exasperated; it means taking that word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Irked is a synonym for irritated or bothered.

clue.text: More for one with small part

blocks.note: first meaning: additional
second meaning: a film actor with a minor non-speaking role

explanation.walkthrough: An extra in a film appears in crowd scenes with no lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means additional and is also the name for a walk-on performer in a film or show.

clue.text: Perhaps dirt makes apparent where washing stopped

definitions.note: describes the lines left, rather than naming them

indicators.note: perhaps hints at a possible alternative arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grime shows exactly where a careless wash ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a description: grime makes visible the line where washing stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the dirty line on a bath or neck marking the limit of the water or the wash.
